KR.read: Korea's bath & shower segment now has a domestic retail size for the first time: US$357.35mn (2025, RETAIL, LOW confidence, Expert Market Research), on a scope EMR describes as shower gel/bubble wash, bath salts, bar soap and bath bombs - narrower than a full bath & shower category, and EMR does not state channel coverage or duty-free treatment. A separate HIGH-confidence MFDS PRODUCTION figure exists for the wider '인체 세정용' (personal/body cleansing) product type, KRW 2.077tn in 2024 (~US$1.405bn), but that type bundles facial foam cleansers and body wash together and is explicitly wider than bath & shower proper - the MFDS release's own narrower '목욕용 제품류' (bath preparations) line is only KRW 130bn (2024), far smaller. These three readings should not be reconciled into one figure; they measure different things. The export figure (US$0.59bn, 2025, EXPORT_FOB, HIGH, MFDS via Yonhap/Korea Herald, 'body cleansing products') is unchanged and remains the only trade-flow figure.
KR.trend: Two growth reads now exist, on different bases: a PRODUCTION-basis +9.88% YoY for 2024 (ESTIMATE confidence, derived from two adjacent years in the same MFDS annex table for the wider 인체 세정용 type - factory-gate output, not retail demand), and a LOW-confidence RETAIL forecast of 2.10% CAGR (2026-2035, Expert Market Research) on the narrower bath-products scope. The gap between a high-single-digit production read and a low-single-digit retail forecast is consistent with the two describing different scopes and different bases, not a contradiction to resolve.
KR.caveats: None of the three size figures share a scope: EMR's bath-products retail figure, the MFDS wider cleansing-type production figure, and the MFDS narrower bath-preparations line are three different measures of overlapping-but-distinct things. The +9.88% growth figure is PRODUCTION basis (factory-gate, ESTIMATE confidence) and should not be read as retail demand growth.

IN.read: India's bath & shower segment now has data, but its own two IMARC figures are internally impossible: IMARC's 'bath & shower products' total (US$1.8bn, 2025, RETAIL, LOW), which IMARC itself says includes bath soap, is smaller than IMARC's own separate 'bath soap' figure for the same year (US$3,406.3mn, 2025, RETAIL, LOW) - a component reading 1.9x larger than the whole it is supposed to sit inside. MarkNtel's independent bath-soap-only figure (US$3.54bn, 2024, RETAIL, LOW) corroborates IMARC's soap figure within about 4%, reinforcing that IMARC's 'wider category' total is the outlier, not the soap figures. No organised-vs-unorganised coverage is stated by any of the three sources.
IN.trend: Forecast CAGRs mirror the same split: IMARC's bath-and-shower total forecasts 3.80% (2026-2034, LOW) while IMARC's own bath-soap-only figure forecasts a faster 4.88% over the identical window, and MarkNtel's bath-soap CAGR is 3.16% (2025-2030, LOW). No growth_yoy figure exists for India bath & shower - this remains an open research gap (three separate research attempts, including a company-results sweep, did not find a defensible single-year observed rate).
IN.caveats: The IMARC 'bath & shower products' total should be treated with real caution given it is smaller than its own stated bath-soap-alone subset - a mathematical impossibility, not just a definitional gap. The two corroborating bath-soap-only figures (IMARC, MarkNtel) are the better-supported anchor for that narrower slice, but a clean 'whole bath & shower category' figure (soap + wash + additives) does not currently exist on file. growth_yoy remains a standing gap.

combined.read: Korea has one LOW-confidence RETAIL size read for bath & shower (US$357.35mn, 2025, narrower 'bath products' scope) and a separate HIGH-confidence EXPORT_FOB figure (US$0.59bn, 2025). India has three RETAIL candidates that do not reconcile with each other (US$1.8bn total that is internally contradicted by its own US$3,406.3mn bath-soap component, plus a corroborating US$3.54bn bath-soap-only MarkNtel figure), so there is no single India value_usd_bn clean enough to set against Korea's figure - a KR-vs-IN size comparison is not attempted here. Bath & shower is not one of the segments flagged as corridor-relevant in config/corridor.yaml (that list covers skincare, sun_care, colour_cosmetics, hair_care, and dermocosmetics), and no data point on either side carries a [CORRIDOR] tag, so no K-beauty-in-India read applies to this segment.
